description: agent_cost/readers/claude.py's parse_session_facts, when usage.cache_creation is a dict, computes leftover = cache_creation_input_tokens - (ephemeral_5m + ephemeral_1h) and emits that leftover as an additional cache_write_unknown fact if it is positive (readers/claude.py lines ~104-112). Both existing tests (test_cache_creation_ttl_breakdown_present, test_cache_creation_without_ttl_breakdown_is_unknown) only cover the two extremes -- a breakdown dict that exactly accounts for the total, and no breakdown dict at all -- so the partial-breakdown case (a cache_creation dict present but its two counters summing to less than cache_creation_input_tokens) is a real, reachable code path with no test asserting what fact(s) it produces.
title: No test exercises the partial-TTL-breakdown leftover branch of parse_session_facts

description: agent_cost/aggregate.py's _STATUS_RANK defines a full three-way order (unpriced=0 < lower_bound=1 < priced=2) that build_rows() uses to downgrade a row's pricing_status to the worst status among its facts. tests/test_aggregate.py's test_build_rows_mixed_priced_and_unpriced_marks_row_unpriced only exercises the unpriced-vs-priced half (mixing an unpriced fact with a normally-priced one). No test in this suite builds a row from a mix of a lower_bound fact (e.g. cache_write_unknown) and a plain priced fact in the same group-by bucket to confirm the row ends up "lower_bound" rather than "priced" -- that half of the ranking is currently confirmed only by reading _STATUS_RANK/build_rows directly (see OBS-010).
title: No test exercises the lower_bound-vs-priced half of build_rows' pricing_status ranking

description: Independently re-checked three README claims that this corpus's observations rely on, against the actual current rates.json/code, looking specifically for a case where the README's prose and the catalog/implementation had drifted apart: (1) "the row also carries a credits figure" is scoped to Codex/OpenAI models only -- confirmed by reading rates.json's models list: every gpt-5.x/gpt-image-2 model entry carries credits_per_mtok, and no claude-* model entry does, so Claude rows never carry a non-zero credits value; (2) "all Claude usage is priced at standard rates" (no batch discount signal) -- confirmed rates.json has exactly one flat rate per (model, period), no batch-specific field anywhere in the schema build_model_entry reads; (3) Codex's `total_tokens == input_tokens + output_tokens` claim (reasoning_output_tokens is a sub-breakdown, not additional) is stated in parse_rollout_facts's own docstring and is consistent with the reader code only ever emitting an "output" fact from output_tokens, never reasoning_output_tokens, directly. No statement contradicting current rates.json/code was found for these three checks; this is not a claim that the corpus's five topics are drift-free overall, only that these three specific cross-checks came back clean.
evidence_ref: README.md#What this measures, and what it doesn't; agent_cost/rates.json; agent_cost/readers/codex.py#parse_rollout_facts
title: Re-checked README's pricing claims against rates.json/code for this corpus's five topics; no drift found
